finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: expression with more than MAX_SIZE opening symbols
finding.assumptions: The stack size is fixed at MAX_SIZE and there is no check to prevent pushing more than MAX_SIZE elements.

parsed.change_summary: Added a check to prevent pushing more than MAX_SIZE elements onto the stack.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The trigger described in the finding no longer works because the code now checks if the stack is full before pushing a new element. If the stack is full, the function returns false, preventing a buffer overflow.
parsed.behavior_changes: The function now returns false if the expression contains more than MAX_SIZE opening symbols, which was not the case before.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the push() implementation (lines 25‑28) and the is_full() helper (lines 20‑22). The push() function performs an explicit overflow check before writing to the stack array, preventing any out‑of‑bounds write. No other code path bypasses this check, and the stack is initialized with top = -1, so the maximum index written is 99, which is within the 100‑element array. Therefore the reported buffer overflow cannot occur.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The expressions are hardcoded and not user-controlled, but if they were, this could lead to OS command injection.

parsed.change_summary: No changes were made to the code as the reported vulnerability (CWE-78: OS Command Injection) does not apply to the given code fragment. The expressions being checked are hardcoded and do not involve any shell command execution.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The trigger described in the finding (expression containing shell metacharacters) does not apply to the given code fragment. The expressions being checked are hardcoded and do not involve any shell command execution. Therefore, the trigger cannot be used to inject OS commands.

parsed.refutation_attempt: 1) Checked whether the untrusted source "expression" is ever used as a format string or argument to a system call. The only sink is printf, but the format string is the constant "%d\n" on lines 67-71, so no injection path exists. 2) Verified that the expression is only read character‑by‑character in is_balanced (lines 40-64) and never passed to any external command or shell. 3) Confirmed that no other functions (e.g., system, exec, popen) are invoked with the expression. 4) No conditional checks or sanitization are required because the format string is constant and the expression is not used as a command. Thus the reported OS command injection claim is unfounded.
